name: Redfin Inc.

financialHealth.envelopeDisclaimer: INTERPRETIVE ONLY — latest filing is 5 quarters old (envelope requires <= 2); not a current validated assessment.

domainRelevance: Redfin operates as a technology-enabled residential real estate brokerage and marketplace, capturing transaction-level signals on housing demand, inventory velocity, and price discovery across 90+ U.S. metropolitan areas. Its proprietary data on days-on-market, offer acceptance rates, and price trends serves as a leading indicator of housing-market liquidity and consumer confidence in the population domain. The company's iBuying segment (Redfin Now) adds direct inventory exposure and cash-flow volatility tied to home price appreciation and mortgage-rate sensitivity.
portalRelevance: Redfin's transaction volume, commission revenue per transaction, and iBuying inventory turnover are critical real-time proxies for residential real estate market health and consumer mobility patterns. Its exposure to mortgage-rate swings (30-year and 15-year FRED series) and housing-inventory constraints makes it a leading indicator of population-domain stress; rising days-on-market and declining offer acceptance rates signal demand destruction before macro housing starts decline. For financial-intelligence models, Redfin's quarterly guidance revisions and same-market transaction trends offer 4–8 week lead signals on housing-market inflection points that cascade into consumer spending, labor mobility, and regional economic divergence.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly transaction volume and days-on-market by metro (disclosed in quarterly earnings call and 10-Q Item 1 business metrics)
Offer acceptance rate and price-per-square-foot trends (proprietary Redfin data index published monthly on investor relations site)
iBuying inventory turnover and gross margin per home sold (10-K Item 1A risk factors and MD&A segment reporting)
Mortgage-rate sensitivity via 30-year and 15-year FRED series correlation to transaction velocity (inferred from earnings guidance revisions tied to rate moves)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: HELIX phase classification based on revenue growth trajectory, gross margin expansion/contraction, and cash burn rate (quarterly 10-Q analysis)
iBuying segment profitability inflection: gross margin per home sold vs. inventory holding costs and price appreciation risk (MD&A segment disclosure)
Commission revenue per transaction trend and market-share gains/losses vs. Zillow, Realty.com, and traditional brokers (industry-report and earnings call)
Cash runway and debt covenant compliance given iBuying cash-flow volatility (10-K Item 7 liquidity analysis and 8-K debt facility amendments)

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Distress signature: declining transaction volume + rising days-on-market + iBuying inventory write-downs + commission rate compression (pattern match vs. 2022–2023 housing downturn)
Growth inflection: accelerating transaction volume + margin expansion in iBuying + market-share gains in high-growth metros (pattern match vs. 2021 housing boom)
Sector contagion: mortgage-rate shock propagation to Redfin's transaction velocity within 2–4 weeks; cross-domain stress from consumer credit tightening (FRED MORTGAGE30US correlation analysis)
Competitive threat: Zillow's iBuying scale and Opendoor's cash position vs. Redfin's smaller iBuying footprint and higher per-home acquisition costs (industry-report and 10-K Item 1A)

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Investment thesis: long-duration play on housing-market recovery and iBuying margin inflection; short-duration hedge on mortgage-rate shock via inverse correlation to 30-year FRED series
Risk management: position sizing tied to iBuying inventory turnover and gross margin; stop-loss if days-on-market exceed 90-day rolling average by >15%
Engagement strategy: quarterly earnings-call monitoring for guidance revisions tied to rate moves; board-level tracking of iBuying profitability roadmap and capital allocation discipline
Hedging: consider short housing-futures or long-volatility positions if mortgage rates spike; monitor Redfin's debt refinancing windows and covenant headroom

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Trade execution: initiate long position on Redfin if iBuying gross margin inflects positive and transaction volume accelerates; size 2–3% of portfolio given volatility

Portfolio rebalancing: reduce exposure if mortgage rates rise >50 bps in single quarter and days-on-market trend deteriorates; rotate proceeds to mortgage-rate-insensitive real estate services (e.g., title, escrow)
Monitoring setup: daily tracking of Redfin's proprietary data index (published on investor relations site); weekly correlation analysis vs. FRED mortgage rates and housing starts
Engagement: attend quarterly earnings calls; request investor-relations briefing on iBuying profitability timeline and capital-allocation priorities

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Earnings validation: compare quarterly transaction volume, days-on-market, and iBuying gross margin vs. prior guidance; flag if variance >10%
Price action: monitor RDFN stock price reaction to earnings and rate moves; validate thesis if stock outperforms during rate-decline periods and underperforms during rate-spike periods
Filing delta: track changes in 10-K Item 1A risk factors (iBuying inventory risk, mortgage-rate sensitivity); flag any 8-K debt covenant amendments or credit facility downgrades
Macro correlation: measure rolling 4-week correlation between RDFN price and FRED MORTGAGE30US; recalibrate if correlation weakens (signal of competitive or operational deterioration)

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Model update: recalibrate HELIX phase transition probabilities based on realized iBuying margin inflection timing; adjust if margin inflection lags rate decline by >2 quarters
Signal reweight: increase weight on days-on-market trend vs. transaction volume if days-on-market proves more predictive of earnings revisions
Sector prior update: update housing-market stress priors based on Redfin's transaction velocity leading-indicator accuracy; measure lag vs. HOUST and NEWMVS FRED series
Competitive positioning: track Zillow and Opendoor iBuying metrics quarterly; adjust Redfin thesis if competitors' gross margins exceed Redfin's by >200 bps for 2+ consecutive quarters

suppliers.name: Amazon Web Services Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Redfin's technology platform and data analytics infrastructure run on AWS cloud services, including compute, storage, and machine-learning services for real-time transaction processing and market-trend analysis. AWS provides the scalability required for Redfin's proprietary data index and mobile app serving 90+ metropolitan markets. Dependency is critical for uptime and latency-sensitive transaction matching; any AWS outage directly impacts Redfin's brokerage and iBuying operations.

suppliers.name: Opendoor Technologies Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Opendoor is a pure-play iBuyer (instant home-buying platform) with larger geographic footprint and higher transaction volume than Redfin Now. Opendoor's business model is capital-intensive and highly sensitive to home-price appreciation; gross margins are structurally lower than Redfin's brokerage business. Redfin's hybrid model (brokerage + iBuying) provides revenue diversification that Opendoor lacks. Competitive threat is primarily in iBuying market share and gross-margin compression.

suppliers.name: National Association of Realtors (NAR)
suppliers.relationshipNote: NAR represents 1.4M+ traditional real estate agents and sets industry standards (MLS access, commission norms, ethical codes). Redfin's low-commission model (1% vs. NAR-affiliated agents' 2.5–3%) directly threatens NAR members' revenue. NAR's 2023 antitrust settlement (eliminating commission-splitting rules) creates structural headwinds for traditional agents but tailwinds for Redfin's value proposition. Regulatory and competitive dynamics are tightly coupled.

suppliers.name: CoreLogic Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: CoreLogic provides property data, valuation models, and title/escrow services to real estate platforms including Redfin. Redfin integrates CoreLogic's automated valuation models (AVMs) and property-history data into its platform for home-price estimation and risk assessment. CoreLogic is a critical data supplier; any degradation in data quality or AVM accuracy directly impacts Redfin's pricing confidence and iBuying profitability. Relationship is contractual and ongoing.

suppliers.name: Fannie Mae (Federal National Mortgage Association)

Fannie Mae's policy shifts (e.g., loan-level price adjustments, credit-score overlays) affect borrower qualification and housing demand. Redfin monitors Fannie Mae's quarterly earnings and policy announcements for rate-path signals.

patent.noveltyAnchor: Dynamic phasic repricing trigger keyed to network fee effective-date metadata rather than manual billing cycle, with per-vertical interchange qualification scoring to minimize downgrade exposure.

programMatch: NSF Future of Work at the Human-Technology Frontier
grant.angle: Frame as adaptive financial infrastructure research: real-time payment cost contingency learning systems that reduce systemic merchant margin volatility, with the neural habit-rigidity model as the formal dynamical reference.

investment.thesis: Processors with demonstrated interchange optimization automation (real-time qualification scoring, dynamic rate-table patching) will sustain net revenue yield through network fee cycles; those without show lagged margin compression detectable 1-2 quarters post-schedule change—a timing arbitrage opportunity in Shift4 vs. peers.

instruments: FOUR long/short relative to payment processor peers on yield compression signal
